answer: An agent economy can resist sybil floods by making identity expensive to multiply. Before an agent may attest or grade, it must lock a slashable deposit that serves as its anchor: if later audits show one operator minted a cluster of shells, those bonds are burned and the cluster is barred. Across an ocean of applicants the outlay scales with every extra persona, so stuffing the roll quickly turns unprofitable. Voting weight then accrues only through a cedar-slow trail of peer-checked work, so influence follows proven history rather than raw headcount.
